title: Student assembly and spontaneous demonstration at Université Nazi Boni
scope: University-campus assembly and demonstration; whether the meeting or march was open to the general public is not reported.
organizer: Coalition of student association/union groups and class delegates, as reported by Burkina24 from AIB.
participants_original: No turnout estimate or numerical attendance is reported in the opened account.
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown: the report gives no count, and the campus setting does not establish public access or a gathering of at least 50.

start_date.summary: Burkina24 reports that a student assembly on Thursday 13 January ended in a spontaneous demonstration and clashes.

location.summary: The account locates the episode at Université Nazi Boni in Bobo-Dioulasso.

organizer.summary: The report identifies a coalition of student associations and class delegates; its details are attributed to AIB.

demands.summary: The reported agenda involved academic-year delays, five-year student suspensions, FONER funding delays and education reforms. The report does not establish whether these were addressed to national government/policy authorities or university administration; no demand category is assigned.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No numerical estimate or evidence of general-public access; threshold remains unknown.

protester_violence.summary: S024 describes clashes, barricades and burning tires but does not permit a confident actor-specific violence attribution in this draft summary. S025 reports an alleged student seizure and beating of an agent via a government spokesperson, but the incident date and connection to 13 January are unclear; retain as an attributed, unresolved counteraccount.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The report describes police pursuit/tear gas following the campus demonstration, supporting an attempted dispersal.

state_response.arrests.summary: No arrest of a protest participant is established. S025 reports a government spokesperson’s account of police extracting an agent and students demanding his handover, but does not establish a protester arrest.

state_response.beatings.summary: No state beating of a demonstrator is established. The alleged beating in S025 is attributed to students and incident linkage is unclear.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No response meeting or agreed formal discussion is reported; value remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: No basis to infer a non-response from these reports.

state_response.killings.summary: Neither opened account confirms a state killing in this gathering.

state_response.shootings.summary: S023 is a search-only advocacy-declaration lead alleging live ammunition; this is not verified body evidence. The opened S024/S025 accounts do not establish gunfire in this gathering.

notes: Keep this 13 January campus episode separate from the 19 January publication of the government spokesperson counteraccount, the 20 January organizer detentions mentioned by VOA for the 22 January march, and all post-coup gatherings. The counteraccount in S025 does not establish that the alleged agent incident occurred on 13 January or at the same site. S024 explicitly attributes the event description to AIB; S041 is a search-only AIB-origin lead and is not independent confirmation. S023 is search-only and its live-ammunition allegation is unverified. Public access, numeric threshold, direct state target and exact incident chronology all remain unresolved.
open_questions: Was the assembly open to the general public, and how many people attended?
Were the reported education grievances directed to national government policy or internal university administration?
What date/site did the government spokesperson’s S025 account describe, and was it part of this episode?
Is there independently verified evidence of protester violence or live-ammunition use?

title: Movement-associated 22 January march and demonstrations
location: Ouagadougou (where VOA reports around 300 downtown); contemporary reports also mention separate gatherings in Bobo-Dioulasso, Kaya and other cities, with no city-specific attendance estimates beyond Ouagadougou.
scope: Movement-associated, multi-city protest call. Whether this is one national episode or several local episodes remains pending unit review; the Ouagadougou count and response are not transferred to other locations.
organizer: Mouvement Sauvons le Burkina Faso is identified as the call’s organizer; local co-organizer details are not established for every city.
participants_original: VOA reports hundreds marching in cities across Burkina Faso and specifically around 300 protesters gathered in downtown Ouagadougou shortly before 9 a.m.; no separate count is supplied for other cities.
threshold_50_evidence: Ouagadougou alone is reported at around 300, which supports a public-gathering threshold at that site without creating an exact count. Other cities have no verified city-specific count. Because a national call may include distinct local actions, event unit remains pending.

start_date.summary: Three opened contemporary reports describe the march and demonstrations on 22 January.

location.summary: Opened accounts identify Ouagadougou and describe demonstrations in other cities; S008 gives the around-300 count only for downtown Ouagadougou. S001/S003 mention Bobo-Dioulasso and Kaya among other local actions.

organizer.summary: The Ouagadougou march is associated with Mouvement Sauvons le Burkina Faso; local organization elsewhere is not fully described.

demands.summary: Sources distinguish dissatisfaction with the Burkina Faso government’s handling of insecurity and the restriction on the march from solidarity with Mali. The domestic security/rights grievances are relevant to the own-state target; Mali solidarity alone is not. A resignation demand appears only in search-only S005 and is not used as verified evidence.

participants_original.summary: VOA’s around-300 estimate refers specifically to downtown Ouagadougou. Its countrywide “hundreds” wording does not supply counts by other city.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported around 300 in Ouagadougou supports threshold there; the other-city counts remain unknown.

protester_violence.summary: Burkina24 reports protesters throwing stones and other objects and clashing with security forces during the 22 January protest wave; this is not geographically disaggregated enough to assign to every city.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Reports describe police use of tear gas and a flashbang/flash grenade to disperse or break up the Ouagadougou crowd and police preventing the group from reaching Place des Nations. This supports attempted dispersal even if the crowd did not immediately cease.

state_response.arrests.summary: The report mentions two organizers detained on 20 January, before the 22 January march. They are not coded as event arrests; no 22 January arrest is established.

state_response.beatings.summary: These opened reports do not establish state beatings of protesters in the 22 January event; unknown is retained.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No meeting or agreed formal discussion is documented; absence from these reports does not establish ignore or a confirmed absence.

state_response.ignore.summary: The reports document police action but do not establish whether government officials ignored the demands.

state_response.killings.summary: No state killing is established for this event.

state_response.shootings.summary: The reported tear gas and flashbang are not gunfire; no shooting is established.

notes: The Ouagadougou crowd estimate is around 300 and belongs only to that city. Other cities and their counts stay unknown. S001 reports stones/objects and clashes during the wave without a reliable city-by-city attribution. Police tear gas/flashbang in Ouagadougou are attempted dispersal. The two organizer detentions occurred 20 January and are not event arrests. The physical end is unknown; do not set it to the last report, city dispersal, or month end. S005’s captured excerpt identifies Saturday 22 January 2022 and a resignation demand, but the exact URL also appears as search-only canonical Burkina Faso 2021-01 S009; its body was not observed and it is not independent confirmation. Preserve the cross-year pointer and do not use its search-only demand as verified evidence. S010 is an explicit HTTP 403; S016 is held by a scoped Le Monde alias rule; other publishers’ opened reporting is used.
open_questions: Should the nation-wide movement call be one event or separate local site events under the original event rules?
What were turnout and episode boundaries in each city beyond Ouagadougou?
What was the physical cessation time in each locality?
Is the S005 resignation demand documented in an accessible body, and which month should carry the cross-year duplicate pointer?

title: Post-takeover gathering at Place de la Nation, Ouagadougou
location: Place de la Nation/Place des Nations, central Ouagadougou.
scope: A spontaneous public pro-junta gathering observed at the square on 25 January; reports likely concern the same gathering, but participant estimates are absent in the opened articles.
organizer: Organizer of the spontaneous gathering is not established. The Movement to Save Burkina Faso and partner associations separately announced a later press conference at the same square; that announcement is not evidence they organized the gathering.
participants_original: Burkina24 describes several young people/demonstrators; Anadolu reports a gathering underway but gives no count. No numeric estimate appears in the opened accounts.
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Neither opened article gives a count; “several” does not establish 50. Le Pays S054 was a search-only lead associated with a preview suggesting hundreds and a democracy/elections appeal, but the body could not be retrieved and that preview is not field evidence.

start_date.summary: Both opened reports are dated 25 January and describe a pro-junta gathering underway at Place de la Nation.

location.summary: Both reports locate attendees at the central Place de la Nation/Place des Nations in Ouagadougou.

organizer.summary: The gathering is described as spontaneous. A separate afternoon press conference was announced by Mouvement Sauvons le Burkina Faso and partner associations; organization of the gathering itself remains unknown.

demands.summary: Anadolu quotes one named participant, Cédric Sawadogo, expressing a wish for Burkina Faso to turn toward countries such as Russia and no longer France; this is an attributed own-state foreign-policy change request, not merely a generic pro-coup statement. Separately, Burkina24 attributes to OSC leader Abdoul Karim Baguian (Lota) proposals for unity/reconciliation and army work with the population, including former President Kaboré. Burkina24’s separate phrase asking Damiba to follow Mali is too unspecified to infer a foreign-policy content. The schema has no foreign-policy-specific demand code; political_behavior_process is a provisional broad mapping for coordinator review.

participants_original.summary: Opened accounts say several demonstrators/youths or describe a gathering, without a numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No opened account establishes 50. S054 remains search_only after tool Cache miss and pre-HTTP DNS failure; the preview is not count evidence.

protester_violence.summary: Neither opened account establishes demonstrator violence; with no affirmative evidence, retain unknown rather than no_explicit.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No meeting or agreed formal discussion is established.

state_response.ignore.summary: No basis to infer ignore from silence.

state_response.killings.summary: No state killing is established for this event.

state_response.shootings.summary: No gunfire is established for this event.

notes: Keep this gathering distinct from the 22 January movement march, the 23–24 January military mutiny/coup events, and the 24 January bystander/waiting lead S046. The explicit policy request in S018 is one named attendee’s statement; it is not assigned to the whole crowd. Pro-coup support by itself is not treated as a demand. S013’s Mali-path phrase and individual domestic proposals are attributed separately. S054 Le Pays could not be read: its web.open returned Cache miss and an exact same-URL ordinary HTTPS attempt failed DNS before HTTP; no publisher denial is inferred. Search-preview indications about hundreds and democratic elections remain unverified. S016 is held by the scoped Le Monde rule and no body was requested.
open_questions: Can an accessible contemporary report establish a site-specific crowd count of at least 50?
Did attendees make a democracy/election demand, as the unavailable S054 preview suggested?
What were the gathering’s physical end and any unreported response?
Does the original schema support the provisional political_behavior_process mapping for the quoted foreign-policy request?
